pages.text: The Fission Reactor is the strongest power source in CyberFarm. It burns uranium $(l:nuclear/fuel_rod)Fuel Rods$(/l) to boil water into $(l)Steam$(), and $(l:nuclear/steam_turbine)Steam Turbines$(/l) turn that steam into FE.
It is a cooling tower in $(l)three sizes$(), built from $(item)Reactor Casing$()s, a few $(item)Reactor Port$()s and one $(item)Fission Reactor Controller$(). The scene shows the Small tower.
Bigger towers burn more rods and reach more power:$(br)$(li)$(l)Small$(): 5x5 x 7, 2, 200%$(br)$(li)$(l)Medium$(): 7x7 x 11, 4, 350%$(br)$(li)$(l)Large$(): 9x9 x 15, 8, 500%
pages.title: Building the tower

pages.text: Every tower is a full square floor, then hollow square rings: wide at the bottom and the rim, narrow at the waist. Ring widths in blocks, layer by layer from the bottom:$(br)$(li)$(l)Small$(): 5x5, 5, 5, 3, 3, 3, 5$(br)$(li)$(l)Medium$(): 7x7, 7, 7, 7, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 7, 7$(br)$(li)$(l)Large$(): 9x9, 9, 9, 9, 9, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 9, 9, 9
$(li)Build the floor and the rings out of $(item)Reactor Casing$()s.$(br)$(li)Leave everything $(l)inside$() the rings $(l)empty$(). Blocks outside a narrower ring do not matter.
$(li)Put the $(item)Fission Reactor Controller$() $(l)in the middle of one side of layer 2$() (the first ring above the floor), facing out. It finds the size by itself, trying the largest first.

$(li)Swap shell blocks for $(item)Reactor Port$()s where pipes, cables or hoppers connect. Two are enough: one for water in, one for steam out. Ports go only $(l)in the middle of the four sides$() (see below), or in the floor.

A Large tower moves more water and steam than basic $(l:cables/liquid_pipe)Liquid Pipes$(/l) and $(l:cables/gas_pipe)Gas Pipes$(/l) carry (1,000 mB/t): use $(l)Advanced$() pipes at its water and steam ports.$(br2)$(l)Help with the layout$(): a $(l:basics/multiblock_projector)Multiblock Projector$(/l) shows any size right where you want to build it. You can also $(l)right-click the unfinished$()

$(l)controller$(): drones fly out, each projecting a group of the blocks still to place, and an amber X marks a block in the way. They start from the size you have built the most of (Small if none). Each further click shows the next size; after Large they come back to Small.$(br2)When the tower is

complete it powers up with a deep chime and $(l)turns into a real cooling tower$(): the blocky casings become one faceted, octagonal shell of enamel panels with glowing mint bands. The controller becomes a $(l)panel$() on the surface and every port a glowing $(l)hatch$(), right where a pipe or cable enters the tower.
$(l)Right-click any block of the tower$() to open the reactor.

Reactor Ports are where the outside world connects:$(br)$(li)$(l)Fuel Rods (hoppers, item pipes of other mods)$(): Depleted Fuel Rods$(br)$(li)Water and $(l:nuclear/coolant)Coolant$(/l) ($(l:cables/liquid_pipe)Liquid Pipes$(/l), buckets): Steam, pushed out by itself ($(l:cables/gas_pipe)Gas Pipes$(/l))
pages.title: Ports

pages.text: A port on a wall connects only $(l)outwards$(), on the face where its hatch is: a pipe running past it above or below does not plug in. A port in the floor connects only $(l)from below$().$(br2)$(l)Where ports go.$() On the walls, only in the middle of each side: the tower is drawn with diagonal faces

towards its corners, and a pipe could not reach a port there. On a ring 3 or 5 blocks wide that is the centre block of each side; on rings 7 or 9 wide, the centre block and the one on each side of it. A port nearer a corner leaves the tower $(l)incomplete$(), and the projector marks it as a block in the way. Inside the floor,
ports go anywhere and are reached from below.$(br2)A port in a wall shared by two towers works for the tower that took it first.
$(li)$(l)Left$(): the $(l)water$() tank and the $(l)coolant$() tank (16,000 mB each). Under the coolant tank: the $(l)Dump coolant$() button.$(br)$(li)$(l)Title$(): the size of the tower.
pages.title: The reactor GUI

pages.text: $(li)$(l)Middle$(): 8 Fuel Rod slots (the ones a smaller tower cannot burn are dimmed), the core (one bar per rod, emerald while it burns) and 4 waste slots for Depleted Fuel Rods. Below them, the $(l)temperature$() bar with its red alarm mark, and a status line.

$(li)$(l)Bottom$(): the $(l)power$() buttons, $(l)-$() and $(l)+$().$(br)$(li)$(l)Right$(): the $(l)steam$() tank (16,000 mB). Under it: the $(l)Dump excess steam$() toggle.$(br)Hover the temperature bar to see the heat the core makes, how much it can cool and the steam it makes, all per tick. Hover the power buttons to see the tower's maximum.

$(l)Power$()$(br2)Power goes from $(l)Off$() up to the tower's maximum, in $(l)steps of 50%$(). A new reactor starts $(l)Off$(): insert rods, connect water, then raise the power. Rods only burn while the power is above Off.$(br2)$(l)Dump coolant$()

The coolant tank holds $(l)one kind$() at a time: Coolant or Cryo Coolant. To switch:$(br)$(li)Set the power to $(l)Off$().$(br)$(li)Click the small button $(l)under the coolant tank$(). The whole tank is poured away and lost.$(br)$(li)Pipe in the new coolant.

The button only works while the power is Off; it lights amber when you can use it. With the tank empty the tower cools with plain water, so lower the power before you raise it again.$(br2)$(l)Dump excess steam$()

A toggle $(l)under the steam tank$(), off at first. While it is $(l)on$() (lit), every tick the steam above $(l)8,000 mB$() (half the steam tank) is vented into the air and $(l)lost$(). The turbines still get their steam first.
Turn it on when your turbines cannot take all the steam: the steam tank never fills up, so the reactor keeps cooling instead of overheating. Vented steam makes no FE.

$(li)Each burning rod makes $(l)50 heat per tick at 100% power$(). 4 rods at 250% make 500 heat per tick.$(br)$(li)Each tick some of that heat goes into the $(l)water$(): 1 mB of water takes 1 heat and leaves as 1 mB of $(l)Steam$(). More power means more steam and more FE.
pages.title: Heat and cooling

pages.text: $(li)How much heat can leave each tick depends on the tower size and on the $(l)primary loop$(): the fluid in the coolant tank. With the tank empty it is plain water.$(br)$(li)$(l)Small$(): 150, 375, 900$(br)$(li)$(l)Medium$(): 250, 625, 1,500$(br)$(li)$(l)Large$(): 400, 1,000, 2,400

Heat per tick the tower can move. Coolants wear out while they work: see $(l:nuclear/coolant)Coolant$(/l).$(br2)Heat can only leave when there is $(l)water$() in the water tank and $(l)room$() in the steam tank.

The highest power that does $(l)not$() overheat, with every rod slot of the tower filled. The steam made each tick equals the water used. A $(l:basics/water_pump)Water Pump$(/l) gives 500 mB/t.$(br)$(li)$(l)Small$(): Water, 150%, 150, 1, 26 min 40 s$(br)$(li)$(l)Small$(): Coolant or Cryo, 200% (max), 200, 1, 20 min$(br)$(li)$(l)Medium$(): Water, 100%, 200, 1, 40 min
pages.title: What each tower produces

pages.text: $(li)$(l)Medium$(): Coolant, 300%, 600, 2, 13 min 20 s$(br)$(li)$(l)Medium$(): Cryo Coolant, 350% (max), 700, 2, 11 min 26 s$(br)$(li)$(l)Large$(): Water, 100%, 400, 1, 40 min$(br)$(li)$(l)Large$(): Coolant, 250%, 1,000, 2, 16 min$(br)$(li)$(l)Large$(): Cryo Coolant, 500% (max), 2,000, 4, 8 min

Cryo Coolant gains nothing in a Small tower: Coolant already cools it at full power.$(br2)What that steam gives in FE/t. Each cell reads $(l)turbines needed → FE/t$(), using only turbines of that size:$(br)$(li)$(l)Small, Water$(): 150, 1 → 1,500, 1 → 2,400, 1 → 3,750

$(l)The turbines must take all the steam.$() If they cannot, the steam tank fills, the water has nowhere to go and the core overheats, unless $(l)Dump excess steam$() is on. A turbine also stops when its FE has nowhere to go.

Heat that cannot leave stays in the core, and the $(l)temperature$() rises.$(br)$(li)Above $(l)80%$() an $(l)alarm$() rings and the GUI flashes $(o)OVERHEATING!$(). Lower the power, add water or coolant, or make room for the steam (more turbines, or Dump excess steam).
pages.title: Overheating and meltdown

pages.text: $(li)At $(l)100%$() the core $(l)melts down$(): the rods are destroyed, the tower $(l)explodes$() and the area around it becomes heavily $(l:nuclear/radiation)radioactive$(/l) for a long time. The blast strength and whether it breaks blocks are set in the common config ($(o)Meltdown Explosion Power$(), $(o)Meltdown Destroys Blocks$()).

How fast it goes depends on how much heat is left over. One power step too high can take minutes. A Large tower at 500% that runs out of water or Cryo Coolant melts down in about $(l)6 seconds$().$(br2)An idle core cools down slowly by itself.
$(l)No escape$(): breaking the controller or any block of the tower while the temperature is above 80% does not save you. The core melts down anyway. Set the power to Off and let it cool first.

$(li)$(l)*Tower incomplete$()*: Check the layout; the drones or a Multiblock Projector show what is missing.$(br)$(li)$(l)*Off: raise the power$()$(o): Press +$()*.$(br)$(li)$(l)*Ready: insert Fuel Rods$()*: Put Fuel Rods in the slots the tower uses.
pages.title: Troubleshooting

pages.text: $(li)$(l)Steam tank full$(): Add turbines, give their FE somewhere to go, or turn on Dump excess steam.$(br)$(li)$(l)Temperature climbing$(): Lower the power, check the water supply and the coolant level.

$(li)$(l)Waste slots full$(): The spent rods wait in the core and it $(l)leaks radiation$(). Pull the waste out with a hopper under a Reactor Port in the floor, or an item pipe on a wall port and treat it in a $(l:nuclear/waste_reprocessor)Waste Reprocessor$(/l).
$(li)$(l)Coolant running out$(): Cooling falls to the plain water level. Keep a $(l:nuclear/coolant_mixer)Coolant Mixer$(/l) piped in.
